source_refs.note: Example of centripetal force: a main subheading of 3.2 Centripetal force, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 59-59.

blocks.text: In every circular or orbital motion, centripetal force is needed which is provided by some agency.

items: When a ball is whirled in a horizontal circle with the help of a string, then tension in the string provides necessary centripetal force.
For an object placed on a turntable, the friction is the centripetal force.
The gravitational force is the cause of the Earth orbiting around the Sun, Moon and artificial satellites revolving around the Earth.
A normal or perpendicular magnetic force compels a charge particle moving along a straight path into a circular path.

When a vehicle takes turn on a road, it also needs centripetal force which is provided by the friction between the tyres and the road. If the road is slippery, then at high speed, the friction may not be sufficient enough to provided necessary centripetal force. Hence, vehicle will not be able to take turn and may skid or may even be toppled. To overcome this difficulty, the highway road is banked on turns. That is, the outer edge of the track is kept slightly higher than that of the inner edge.

blocks.alt: A pack of colourful racing cars sweeps round a curve of a grey race track. The track surface is tilted: its outer edge, at the top by the wall, is higher than its inner edge, where a white line and a pale apron run along the inside of the turn.
blocks.caption: Tid-bits (PDF page 61): racing cars on a banked track (original drawing after the photograph printed in the textbook).

blocks.text: Banked tracks are needed for turns that are taken so quickly that friction alone cannot provide energy for centripetal force.
blocks.title: Tid-bits

blocks.text: Friction does not provide energy here: it provides the centripetal force itself. The sentence should read: friction alone cannot provide the necessary centripetal force.
